title: Ten lights
hook: ten emanations through which the Infinite relates to the world

segments.voice: Yesterday, Ein Sof: God without end, beyond every description. Your line was without end. And it left a question hanging: how does the endless touch a world with edges? Day one thousand one hundred seventy-five.

"Thine, O LORD, is the greatness, and the power, and the glory, and the victory, and the majesty." King David says it in the book of Chronicles, blessing God in front of the whole assembly. It sounds like one long sweep of praise. But slow down and count the nouns. Greatness. Power. Glory. Victory. Majesty. In Hebrew each of those is its own word, and Jewish mystics read them as more than praise. To them it was a list. Names of the ways the one God shows up in the world. That list has a name of its own. Today's word.
screen: `THINE, O LORD, IS THE GREATNESS.` → `COUNT THE NOUNS.` → `NOT JUST PRAISE. A LIST.`

segments.voice: Sefirot. You met the word two days ago in Sefer Yetzirah. In Kabbalah it grows into a whole map: ten lights, or ten emanations, through which Ein Sof, God without end, relates to the world. Turn it four ways. First, the number. Sefer Yetzirah insists on it: ten, it says, and not nine; ten, and not eleven. Not a loose handful. A shape with a definite count. Second, the names. One common order runs: Keter, crown. Chochmah, wisdom. Binah, understanding. Chesed, love. Gevurah, strength. Tiferet, beauty. Netzach, endurance. Hod, splendor. Yesod, foundation. And Malchut, kingship. Listen for David's verse inside it: gevurah, tiferet, netzach, hod. Kabbalists heard those sefirot in that very line. Third, the warning. Ten lights does not mean ten gods. Sefer Yetzirah says their end is bound up in their beginning, like a flame tied to a coal. One fire, many tongues of flame. Kabbalists say again and again that God is one, and the sefirot are how that one God is turned toward us. Fourth, why it matters on an ordinary afternoon. The sefirot are also qualities a person has: love, restraint, balance, steadiness, the ability to bring something into the world. Kabbalists read the human being as built in the same pattern. So the map of how God meets the world doubles as a map of a life. Over the next days, we'll walk it, a few lights at a time, from the top down.
screen: `TEN, AND NOT NINE.` · `CROWN DOWN TO KINGSHIP.` · `A FLAME TIED TO A COAL.` · `A MAP OF A LIFE, TOO.` · then, large: `TEN LIGHTS.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: learn the ten names. Settle, and breathe. On each breath, say one name quietly, from the top down, with its meaning. Keter, crown. Chochmah, wisdom. Binah, understanding. Chesed, love. Gevurah, strength. Tiferet, beauty. Netzach, endurance. Hod, splendor. Yesod, foundation. Malchut, kingship. When you reach the bottom, start again at the top, a little slower. Don't worry about getting the order perfect. Let one of them catch on something in your own life, and stay with that one. The bell holds the time.
Sefirot. The ten lights, or emanations, through which, in Kabbalah, the one God without end relates to the world, from crown to kingship. Today's word.
Your line: ten lights. Today, pick the one name from the ten that caught on something, and notice where it shows up between now and tonight. Day one thousand one hundred seventy-five.

howItsDone: Students of Kabbalah learn the ten sefirot by name and order, often drawn as a diagram, and Hasidic teaching applies them to a person's own character and inner life.

trapdoor: what you thought: ten mystical levels to climb.
what it means: ten lights through which the one God without end relates to the world, and a pattern in each person too.
what a scholar hears: Sefer Yetzirah's "ten and not nine", its flame and coal, and the kabbalists' reading of 1 Chronicles 29:11 as names of the sefirot.

sources.quoted: Thine, O LORD, is the greatness, and the power, and the glory, and the victory, and the majesty

notes: 1 Chronicles 29:11 quoted from the KJV; JPS 1917 reads very closely here, but the KJV wording is the one quoted. The kabbalistic reading of gedulah, gevurah, tiferet, netzach, hod as sefirot is stated as what kabbalists heard; please confirm.

Order of the ten given as 'one common order' with Keter at the top; some lists use Da'at in place of Keter. English glosses (love, strength, beauty, endurance, splendor, foundation, kingship) are common but not the only ones.
Sefer Yetzirah 1:4 ('ten and not nine, ten and not eleven') and 1:7 (end embedded in beginning, like a flame bound to a coal) are paraphrased; verse numbering varies by version.
Hook: 'in front of the whole assembly' follows 1 Chronicles 29:10.
